functions.name: area
functions.description: Get a Numpy array of surface area of the liner elements.

functions.name: beta
functions.description: Get a Numpy array of liner system beta angle. This is defined as the angle between the element local system x-axis and the material system x-axis. In radians measured counter-clockwise from the element local x-axis.

functions.name: component_id
functions.description: Get a NumPy array of the ID of liner component id.

functions.name: density
functions.description: Get a NumPy array of the density of liner elements.

functions.name: depth_factor
functions.description: Get a Numpy array of the depth factor at which stresses have been recovered. The depth equals Ft/2 where t is the liner element thickness. F values equal to +1.0 or -1.0 correspond to the outer/inner liner surface. The outer surface is defined by the positive z-direction of the local liner element system. F values of 0.0 corresponds to the liner mid-surface. The depth factor can be modified with the \(structure liner recover stress\) command.

functions.name: element_type
functions.description: Get a Numpy array of the name of the finite-element type used by the liner elements. The possible types for liner elements are ‘cst’, ‘csth’, ‘dkt’, ‘dkt-cst’, and ‘dkt-csth’.

functions.name: embedded
functions.description: Get a Numpy array of the embedded flag. True denotes that the liner element is embedded.

functions.name: extra
functions.signature: itasca.structure.linerarray.extra(slot: int) -> array float{liner} or float{liner,3}
functions.description: Get the liner extra data in the given slot as an array. Extra variables accessed by array must be of type float or vec.

functions.name: force
functions.description: Get a Numpy array of the force at each end of the liner using the force-moment sign convention.

functions.name: force_nodal
functions.description: Get a Numpy array of the generalized nodal force acting on the liner at each node. The translational and rotational components of node 1 are given first.

functions.name: id
functions.description: Get a NumPy array of the ID of liner element id.

functions.name: in_group
functions.description: Return liner group membership as a Boolean array.

functions.name: length
functions.description: Get a Numpy array of the length of the liner elements.

functions.name: load
functions.description: Get a Numpy array of the uniform applied distributed load acting on the liner elements in the local y- and z-directions. The x-component of the return value will always be 0.0.

functions.name: local_system
functions.description: Get a NumPy array of the local coordinate system of liner elements.

functions.name: mark
functions.description: Get a NumPy array of the mark flag of liner elements.

functions.name: moment
functions.description: Get a Numpy array of the moment at each end of the liner using the force-moment sign convention.

functions.name: moment_plastic
functions.description: Get a Numpy array of the plastic moment capacity in the liner.

functions.name: normal_dir
functions.description: Get a Numpy array of the direction (unit vector in global system) in which the liner elements are being loaded by the normal coupling spring at each node.

functions.name: normal_disp
functions.description: Get a Numpy array of the displacement magnitude in the normal coupling spring at each node. The coupling spring lies in the tangent plane of the liner surface. The direction in which force is acting is given by \(normal_dir\) method.

functions.name: normal_state
functions.description: Get a Numpy array of the yield state of the coupling spring at each side of each node. Return values 1, 2 and 3 denotes never yielded, yielding now, or yielded in the past, respectively. Side 1 and 2 of node 1 are given first.

functions.name: normal_stiffness
functions.description: Get a Numpy array of the normal coupling spring stiffness of the liner element for each side of the liner.

functions.name: normal_strength
functions.description: Get a Numpy array of the normal coupling spring tensile strength for each side of the liner element.

functions.name: normal_stress
functions.description: Get a Numpy array of the stress magnitude in the normal coupling spring at each node. The coupling spring lies in the tangent plane of the liner surface. The direction in which force is acting is given by \(normal_dir\) method.

functions.name: poisson
functions.description: Get a Numpy array of the Poisson’s ratio of the elements.

functions.name: pos
functions.description: Get a NumPy array of the current position of liner elements.

functions.name: pressure
functions.description: Get a Numpy array of the uniform pressure acting on the liner elements. A positive value acts in the z-direction of the element local system.

functions.name: prop_anis
functions.signature: itasca.structure.linerarray.prop_anis() -> (membrane: tuple of float, bending: tuple of float)
functions.description: Get the anisotropic material properties. Material-stiffness coefficients c’11, c’12, c’13, c’22, c’23, c’33 are returned for both the membrane and bending stiffnesses in that order. If the element does not have anisotropic properties, zeros are returned.

returns.type: (membrane: tuple of float, bending: tuple of float)

functions.name: prop_ortho
functions.signature: itasca.structure.linerarray.prop_ortho() -> (membrane: tuple of float, bending: tuple of float)
functions.description: Get the orthotropic material properties. Material-stiffness coefficients c’11, c’12, c’13, c’22, c’23, c’33 are returned for both the membrane and bending stiffnesses in that order. If the element does not have orthotropic properties, zeros are returned.

returns.type: (membrane: tuple of float, bending: tuple of float)

functions.name: prop_type
functions.description: Get a Numpy array of the material property type. Possible return values are ‘isotropic’, ‘orthotripc’, and ‘anisotropic’.

functions.name: resultant
functions.signature: itasca.structure.linerarray.resultant(location: int) -> length 8 tuple of array float{liner}
functions.description: Get a Numpy array of stress resultants last calculated for the element at the index \(location\). A \(location\) value of 0 gives the resultant at the element centroid; \(location\) values 1, 2 and 3 give the resultant at the nodes. The components in the return value are: Mx, My, Mxy, Nx, Ny, Nxy, Qx and Qy. Note that stress resultants must be calculated with the \(structure liner recover\) command. See also the \(resultant_valid\) method.

functions.name: resultant_valid
functions.description: Get a Numpy array of of the stress resultant validity flag. True indicates that the stress resultant values are valid. False indicates that resultants have not been calculated or that there has been a change since they were last calculated that would invalidate the results.

functions.name: set_area
functions.description: Set the cross-section area of the elements.

functions.name: set_density
functions.description: Set the density of liner elements.

functions.name: set_extra
functions.signature: itasca.structure.linerarray.set_extra(slot: int, data: array float{liner} or float{liner, 3}) -> None
functions.description: Set the liner extra data in the given slot with an array. Extra variables set by array must be of type float or vec.

functions.name: set_group
functions.signature: itasca.structure.linerarray.set_group(membership: array bool{liner}, group_name: str, slot=1) -> None
functions.description: Set liner group from an array. Where membership True set the corresponding liner to be a member of group group_name in the given slot.

functions.name: set_load
functions.description: Set the uniform applied distributed load acting on the liner elements in the local y- and z-directions. The x-component is ignored on assignment.

functions.name: set_mark
functions.description: Set the mark flag of liner elements.

functions.name: set_moment_plastic
functions.description: Set the plastic moment capacity in the liner.

functions.name: set_normal_stiffness
functions.description: array float{liner,2} -> None. Set the normal coupling spring stiffness of the liner element for each side of the liner.

functions.name: set_normal_strength
functions.description: Set the normal coupling spring tensile strength for each side of the liner element.

functions.name: set_poisson
functions.description: Set the Poisson’s ratio of the elements.

functions.name: set_pressure
functions.description: Set the uniform pressure acting on the liner elements. A positive value acts in the z-direction of the element local system.

functions.name: set_shear_cohesion
functions.description: array float{liner,2} -> None. Set the shear coupling spring cohesion for each side of the liner element.

functions.name: set_shear_friction
functions.description: Set the shear coupling spring friction angle for each side of the liner elements.

functions.name: set_shear_residual
functions.description: array float{liner,2} -> None. Set the shear coupling spring residual cohesion for each side of the liner elements.

functions.name: set_shear_stiffness
functions.description: array float{liner,2} -> None. Set the shear coupling spring stiffness for each side of the liner elements.

functions.name: set_slide
functions.description: Set the large-strain sliding flag. A true value denotes that the large-strain sliding is on.

functions.name: set_slide_tol
functions.description: Set the (shear) coupling spring slide tolerance of the liner elements.

functions.name: set_thermal_expansion
functions.description: Set the thermal expansion coefficient of liner elements.

functions.name: set_thickness
functions.description: Set the element thickness.

functions.name: set_young
functions.description: Set the Youngs modulus of the elements.

functions.name: shear_cohesion
functions.description: Get a Numpy array of the shear coupling spring cohesion for each side of the liner element.

functions.name: shear_dir
functions.description: Get a Numpy array of the direction (unit vector in global system) in which the liner element is being loaded by the shear coupling spring at each node.

functions.name: shear_disp
functions.description: Get a Numpy array of the displacement magnitude in the shear coupling spring at each node. The coupling spring lies in the tangent plane of the liner surface. The direction in which force is acting is given by \(shear_dir\) method.

functions.name: shear_friction
functions.description: Get a Numpy array of the shear coupling spring friction angle for each side of the liner elements.

functions.name: shear_residual
functions.description: Get a Numpy array of the shear coupling spring residual cohesion for each side of the liner elements.

functions.name: shear_state
functions.signature: itasca.structure.linerarray.shear_state() -> (int, int, int, int, int, int)
functions.description: Get a Numpy array of the yield state of the coupling spring at each side of each node. Return values 1, 2 and 3 denotes never yielded, yielding now, or yielded in the past, respectively. Side 1 and 2 of node 1 are given first.

functions.name: shear_stiffness
functions.description: Get a Numpy array of the shear coupling spring stiffness for each side of the liner elements.

functions.name: shear_stress
functions.description: Get a Numpy array of the stress magnitude in the coupling spring at each node. The coupling spring lies in the tangent plane of the liner surface. The direction in which force is acting is given by the \(shear_dir\) method.

functions.name: slide
functions.description: Get a Numpy array of the large-strain sliding flag. A true value denotes that the large-strain sliding is on.

functions.name: slide_tol
functions.description: Get a Numpy array of the (shear) coupling spring slide tolerance of the liner elements.

functions.name: stress
functions.description: Get a Numpy array of the stresses at the current depth factor at the index \(location\). A \(location\) value of 0 gives the stress at the element centroid; \(location\) values 1, 2 and 3 give the stress at the nodes. Stresses are expressed in the global system. Note that compressive stresses are negative.

functions.name: stress_prin
functions.description: Get the resolved principal stress at the current depth factor at the index \(location\). A \(location\) value of 0 gives the stress at the element centroid; \(location\) values 1, 2 and 3 give the stress at the nodes. Returns a vector encoded as (minimum, intermediate, maximum). Note that compressive stresses are negative in FLAC3D.

functions.name: stress_valid
functions.description: Get a Numpy array of the stress validity flag for the element. True indicates that the stresses last calculated at the current depth factor are valid. Galse indicates that stresses have not been calculated, or that there has been a change that invalidates the last stresses calculated.

functions.name: thermal_expansion
functions.description: Get a NumPy array of the thermal expansion coefficient of liner elements.

functions.name: thickness
functions.description: Get a Numpy array of the element thickness.

functions.name: type
functions.description: Get a NumPy array of the type name of liner elements.

functions.name: volume
functions.description: Get a Numpy array of the element volume, or surface area times thickness.

functions.name: ydir
functions.description: Get a Numpy array of the y-axis of the liner elements local system.

functions.name: young
functions.description: Get a Numpy array of the Youngs modulus of the elements. Modifying the value during cycling may be a danger.
